newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: DBS Land sees sustained growth for 1997.
newsitem.headline: DBS Land sees sustained growth for 1997.

text.p: Singapore property and hotel company DBS Land Ltd said it expects to see sustained growth in 1997 after profits advanced to record levels last year.

"Growth was broad-based in both Singapore and from overseas and we expect growth over the next few years to be sustained," Dr Han Cheng Fong, deputy chairman and group chief executive, told a news conference over the weekend.
He said profitability would be helped by developments in Hong Kong, Shanghai and Australia, while the Singapore residential market continued to experience a period of consolidation.
The group's net profits for the year ending December 31, 1996 rose 30.9 percent to Singapore $207.3 million.
The main reason for the strong performance was the rise in profits from property trading by 58 percent to S$193.5 million.

Han said one of DBS Land's main properties, Plaza Singapura, would be closed in the middle of the year for upgrading, but this should be offset by the completion of an office building for lease in the financial district this year.
